name: Effects and 3D Rulebook
summary: Modern effects, shaders and 3D from the effects library, used at the level the user chose and without hurting speed or access.
check: Compare the effects on each page with the effect level in `xslop/DECISIONS.md`.
Lighthouse on mobile and a 4× CPU-throttled recording: no long frames while scrolling.
Turn on reduced motion and disable WebGL (`chrome://flags` or a browser without GPU): fallbacks appear.

rules.title: Effects match the intake answer
rules.text: The effect level the user chose (none, subtle, modern, immersive 3D) caps every effect on the site. Never add 3D or shaders because the brief said "modern" without asking (`effects/levels.md`).

rules.title: One hero effect per page
rules.text: Each page has at most one leading effect, usually in the first screen. Everything else supports it quietly.

rules.title: Restyle every component
rules.text: Installed components take the project's colours, radius, type and spacing tokens. Demo colours, demo text and demo images are removed.

rules.title: Lazy-load heavy effects
rules.text: WebGL, three.js, R3F and Spline load after first paint (dynamic import, `ssr: false`, or on idle/visible), never in the critical path.

rules.title: Render only while visible
rules.text: Animated canvases pause when off screen (IntersectionObserver) and when the tab is hidden.

rules.title: Cap the pixel ratio
rules.text: GPU effects render at `devicePixelRatio` capped at 1.5–2, and lower on small screens.

rules.title: A static fallback
rules.text: Every GPU effect has a poster image or CSS gradient that shows before it loads, if WebGL fails, and for reduced motion.

rules.title: Reduced motion version
rules.text: With `prefers-reduced-motion`, effects stop or become a still frame; text animations show the final text immediately.

rules.title: Content stays real HTML
rules.text: Headlines, labels and links inside effects remain selectable text in the DOM, readable by screen readers and search engines.

rules.title: Test on a mid-range phone
rules.text: Effects are checked on a real mid-range Android phone or with 4× CPU throttling: smooth scroll, INP under 200 ms, no overheating.

rules.title: Install from the official source
rules.text: Components come from their registry (React Bits, 21st.dev) with their licence checked and recorded in the project.

rules.title: Several GPU canvases at once
rules.text: Never more than one WebGL canvas visible at the same time.

rules.title: 3D on every section
rules.text: No 3D object, shader or tilt in every section. Repetition turns a signature into noise.

rules.title: Effects behind body text
rules.text: No moving background behind paragraphs, forms or prices.

rules.title: Cursor replacements in working UI
rules.text: No custom cursors, cursor trails or blob cursors on forms, shops, dashboards or long reading pages.

rules.title: Effects as the LCP element
rules.text: The largest element of the first screen is never a canvas that waits for JavaScript; use a poster or real image.

rules.title: Demo content left in
rules.text: No placeholder images, sample names or lorem text from component demos.

rules.title: React only for an effect
rules.text: Do not add React to a non-React site just to run one animation; rebuild the idea with CSS, GSAP or three.js.

rules.title: Redistributing component libraries
rules.text: Never copy React Bits or 21st.dev component source into a template, kit or skill for sale or redistribution; install per project.
